result:
If I could change one thing, I'd make genuinely good education universally accessible: not just school seats, but curiosity, critical thinking, basic science, media literacy, empathy, and practical skills for every child regardless of where they're born.

My reasoning is that it compounds. Better-educated societies tend to be healthier, more innovative, less easily manipulated, and more able to handle problems like poverty, disease, and climate change. It doesn't fix everything by itself—people still need food, safety, justice, and clean institutions—but it's one of the few changes that strengthens almost every other solution.

That said, I'd hold the choice loosely: if "education" just means test scores, it won't deliver this. The real change would be helping people think clearly and care wisely.
